Origin: Volcan Azul, West Valley, Costa Rica

Producer: Alejo Castro

Elevation: 1500 masl

Process: Anaerobic Natural

Story: Alejo Castro is the fifth generation descendant of renowned coffee pioneers Alejo C. Jimenez and Wilhelm Kahle. Alejo's ancestors planted some of the first specialty coffee plantations in the early 1900s with the aim to produce the best coffee in the world. With over 200 years of family tradition in trading specialty coffee, Alejo's mission for the farm has been exclusively focused on improving coffee quality while making a positive impact on the environment. The highly fertile volcanic soil combined with the mill's impeccable processing methods has produced a history of award-winning coffees in Costa Rica. This coffee from Volcan Azul has a balanced profile with juicy fruit flavours and high sweetness.

products.title: [Rested] SL34, SL28, Ruiru 11, Batian - Washed - Kii AB
products.body_html:
Tastes Like: Blackcurrant, Black Tea, Plum

Origin: Kii Coffee Factory, Kirinyaga, Kenya

Variety: SL-34, SL-28, Ruiru 11, Batian

Producer: Smallholder Producers of Rungeto Farmers Cooperative Society

Elevation: 1,850 masl

Process: Washed


Abstract / Cup Profile Summary

This washed Kenyan coffee centers on blackcurrant and ripe plum, with black tea providing structure through the finish. The fruit character is dark and defined, creating a clean balance of sweetness and tea-like depth.


Farm / Producer / Washing Station

Kii Coffee Factory is one of three washing stations operated by Rungeto Farmers Cooperative Society in Kirinyaga County, near the foothills of Mount Kenya. Smallholder members deliver cherry from their individual farms to Kii, where the coffee is processed collectively as a washing-station lot.


Variety

This lot combines four varieties commonly grown in Kenya. SL-28 and SL-34 are long-established Kenyan selections recognized for their quality potential at elevation, while Ruiru 11 and Batian were developed to improve productivity and resistance to coffee berry disease and coffee leaf rust. Because cherries are combined at the washing station, the varieties are presented as a mixed lot rather than as individually separated components.

products.title: [Rested/Ultralight] Gesha - Natural - Hacienda La Esmeralda, Bosque 3BANC
products.body_html:
Tastes Like: Jasmine, Strawberry, Red Florals

Origin: Bosque lot, Jaramillo Farm, Boquete, Chiriquí, Panama

Variety: Gesha

Producer: The Peterson Family, Hacienda La Esmeralda

Elevation: 1,700+ masl

Process:  Natural with Cold-Room Anaerobic Fermentation and Climate-Controlled Drying (BANC)

Farm / Producer

Hacienda La Esmeralda is the Peterson family's coffee estate in Boquete, Panama. The family expanded into coffee production in the 1980s and purchased Jaramillo Farm in 1997. A Gesha lot from Jaramillo won the 2004 Best of Panama competition, helping bring international attention to the variety.

Bosque 3 BANC comes from the Bosque lot at Jaramillo, above 1,700 meters. The lot has 2.1 hectares in production, with coffee trees averaging 15 years old. Jaramillo's cool, humid mountain conditions, established shade trees, and steep slopes shape the setting in which this coffee grows.

Variety

Gesha, also spelled Geisha, traces its origins to Ethiopia and has become closely associated with Panama's specialty coffee. At high elevations, it can develop delicate floral and stone-fruit aromatics. Jaramillo is an important part of that history, where the Peterson family's separation of individual lots helped reveal the variety's distinctive character.

Processing

Harvested on January 19, 2026, the cherries spent two days pre-drying outdoors on raised beds before four days of fermentation in a sealed stainless-steel tank inside a cold room. They then dried for 41 days in a climate-controlled room with regulated temperature, humidity, and airflow, completing the natural process as whole cherries.

products.title: Landrace - Natural - Danche
products.body_html:
Tastes Like: Blueberries, Tropical, Rhubarb

Origin: Chelbesa, Gedeb, Ethiopia

Variety: Kurume, Wolisho (Ethiopian landraces)

Producer: Smallholder farmers delivering to Danche Station, managed by SNAP Specialty Coffee

Elevation: Approximately 2,200 masl

Process:  Natural

Danche Washing Station

Danche Station serves around 800 farmers in Chelbesa, within Ethiopia’s Gedeb coffee-growing area. Their farms typically cover two to three hectares at an average elevation of about 2,200 meters. Managed by SNAP Specialty Coffee, the station brings these smallholder harvests together for sorting, fermentation, and drying. SNAP also supports producers through agronomy training, including nursery management and growing other crops alongside coffee.

Variety

Kurume is a locally named Ethiopian landrace grown alongside other regional coffee types. Wolisho, also called Welicho, is another landrace associated with Ethiopia’s highlands, distinguished by larger cherries and a broad canopy. Together, they represent part of the local coffee diversity found in Danche’s smallholder lots.

Processing

Whole cherries are fermented in tanks for three days, then spread on raised beds to dry in the sun for 16–21 days. They are turned regularly throughout drying to help the coffee dry evenly.

products.title: Yellow Bourbon - Anaerobic Washed - Quanqing Zou
products.body_html:
Tastes Like: Honeysuckle, Apricot, Black Tea

Origin: Hongfeng Guogei Coffee Estate, Lancang, Yunnan, China

Variety: Yellow Bourbon

Producer: Quanqing Zou (邹泉清)

Elevation: 1,200–1,600 masl

Process:  Anaerobic Washed

HongfengGuogei Coffee Estate

Quanqing Zou, known locally as Zou Jie, is one of the producers behind HongfengGuogei Coffee Estate in Lancang County. The estate takes its name from the local Wa village of Guogei. Zou began working with coffee in 2003 and turned her attention to specialty production in 2016. Her work includes quality assessment, cupping, and developing the estate’s processing methods.

The farm occupies hillsides in Laba Township, where a humid subtropical climate brings ample rainfall and marked differences between daytime and nighttime temperatures. Alongside its own plantings, the estate works with surrounding growers, providing cultivation training and purchasing their coffee. Its variety trials have included Yellow Bourbon, Sarchimor, Pacamara, and Typica.

Processing

This lot uses an anaerobic washed process, combining fermentation with limited oxygen and washed preparation before drying. Its honeysuckle, apricot, and black tea notes bring together floral, stone-fruit, and tea-like elements in the finished cup.

products.title: Gesha - Washed "Flower Machine" - TNT Lab, Digna Nuñez
products.body_html:
Tastes Like: Wisteria, Green Grape, White Peach

Origin: Talamanca Farm, Volcan, Piedra candela, Panama

Variety: Gesha

Producer: Digna Nuñez / Adrian Santiago 

Elevation: 1,450-1,500 masl

Process: Washed and Cold Room Dried (Fermented at 9°C in cherry for 4 days, then depulped and fermented with water and mucilage for 4 more days. Drying: 20 days in the Cold Room.)

 

About the Farm and Producer

Digna Nuñez and her husband, Glaystter Aguilar, established Talamanca Coffee Farm in the 1990s, continuing a family coffee-growing tradition. Glaystter’s parents, Isidro Aguilar and Aloisa Hartman, had begun developing the family farm in the 1960s. Digna and Glaystter built on that foundation by refining cultivation and post-harvest practices while strengthening environmental conservation on the farm. Their sons now contribute to the business, extending the family’s involvement into a fourth generation.

The processing was handled by TNT Lab, a Panama-based processing project known for applying controlled fermentation and drying protocols to selected cherry from partner producers. In this lot, Digna Núñez’s Gesha is paired with TNT Lab’s “Flower Machine” process, placing the focus on a clean but highly aromatic expression of Panama Gesha.

Variety

Gesha, also spelled Geisha, is an Arabica variety strongly associated with Panama’s specialty coffee reputation. It is often valued for its potential for delicate florality, tea-like structure, refined acidity, and stone-fruit aromatics when grown and processed carefully at higher elevations. In this coffee, the variety provides a strong foundation for the wisteria, green grape, and white peach profile while the cold anaerobic washed process adds additional aromatic intensity and sweetness.

Processing

This lot is processed as an anaerobic washed coffee and dried in a cold room. The cherries are fermented at 9°C for 4 days, then depulped and fermented again with water and mucilage for another 4 days before drying for 20 days in the cold room.

This style of low-temperature fermentation can emphasize aromatic precision and layered fruit while slowing down microbial activity compared with warmer fermentations. The washed stage helps preserve clarity and acidity, while the extended cold-room drying supports a more controlled, even finish in the cup.

products.title: Gesha - Natural "Polar Bear" - TNT Lab, Digna Nuñez
products.body_html:
Tastes Like: Pomegranate, Pineapple, Violet

Origin: Talamanca Farm, Piedra Candela, Volcán, Panama

Variety: Gesha

Producer: Digna Nuñez / Adrian Santiago 

Elevation: 1,450-1,500 masl

Process:  Natural - Polar Bear (ultra-slow, temperature-controlled drying)

About the Farm and Producer

Digna Nuñez and her husband, Glaystter Aguilar, established Talamanca Coffee Farm in the 1990s, continuing a family coffee-growing tradition. Glaystter’s parents, Isidro Aguilar and Aloisa Hartman, had begun developing the family farm in the 1960s. Digna and Glaystter built on that foundation by refining cultivation and post-harvest practices while strengthening environmental conservation on the farm. Their sons now contribute to the business, extending the family’s involvement into a fourth generation.

The processing was handled by TNT Lab, a Panama-based processing project known for applying controlled fermentation and drying protocols to selected cherry from partner producers. In this lot, Digna Nuñez’s Gesha is paired with TNT Lab’s “Polar Bear” process, placing the focus on a clean but highly aromatic expression of Panama Gesha.

Variety

Gesha, also spelled Geisha, is an Arabica variety with origins in Ethiopia that became widely recognized through cultivation in Panama. It is valued for its potential for delicate floral and fruit aromatics at higher elevations. Its expression depends on the growing conditions and processing of each lot.

Processing

For Polar Bear, the coffee dries as whole cherries over 28 days, beginning with seven days at 9°C. The temperature then rises in three stages: seven days at 16°C, seven days at 25°C, and seven days at 30°C. This gradual progression from cold to warmer conditions defines TNT Lab’s ultra-slow natural process.

products.title: [Rested/Ultralight] Landrace - Natural - Banko Chelchele
products.body_html:
Tastes Like: Watermelon, Yellow Peach, Floral

Origin: Banko Chelchele, Gedeb, Gedeo, Ethiopia

Variety: 74112, 74110 (Ethiopian Landrace)

Producer: Smallholder farmers in Banko Chelchele

Elevation: 1,900–2,300 masl

Process:  Natural

About Banko Chelchele

Banko Chelchele is a village in Gedeb, within Ethiopia’s Gedeo Zone. The contributing smallholder farmers cultivate coffee at elevations of 1,900–2,300 meters, in fertile, well-drained red clay soils. Annual rainfall ranges from 1,200 to 1,599 millimeters, with harvesting taking place from October through December.

Coffee farming is a central source of income for local households, with cultivation and harvesting knowledge passed between generations. During harvest, farmers handpick ripe cherries and sort them to remove debris and unsuitable fruit before drying.

Variety

74112 is an Ethiopian Arabica selection developed through the Jimma Agricultural Research Center’s work on coffee berry disease resistance and productive varieties. Originating from the Metu-Bishari area, it has a compact growth habit and demonstrated potential for good cup quality.

74110 comes from the same selection program and was also selected for disease resistance and yield potential. Its compact trees produce relatively small leaves, cherries, and seeds. Both varieties illustrate the role of selected Ethiopian coffee populations in cultivation today; their expression in the cup also depends on growing conditions, processing, and roasting.

Processing

Ripe cherries are handpicked, sorted, and dried whole in the sun, with the skin and fruit surrounding the seeds throughout drying. Regular turning helps the cherries dry evenly. After drying and a resting period, the coffee is dry-milled to remove the dried fruit and parchment, revealing the green beans.

Natural processing can encourage pronounced fruit expression. Careful cherry selection and drying help manage fermentation and preserve the coffee’s quality.

products.title: [Rested] Landrace - Anaerobic Washed - Danche
products.body_html:
Tastes Like: Apricot, Plum, Fig

Origin: Chelbesa, Gedeb, Ethiopia

Variety: 74158, 74112 (Ethiopian Landraces)

Producer: Chelbesa Washing Station

Elevation: 2,173 masl

Process:  Washed

Washing Station and Producers

Chelbesa washing station serves around 672 contributing farmers in Gedeb, Ethiopia. These growers cultivate coffee at approximately 2,173 meters above sea level, primarily planting the local 74158 and 74112 varieties. The station brings their cherries together for sorting, pulping, fermentation, and drying.

Variety

74158 is an Ethiopian Arabica selection developed from the country's coffee genetic resources as part of work on resistance to coffee berry disease. It is one of the two varieties reported for this Chelbesa lot.

74112 is a separate Ethiopian Arabica selection from the same wider disease-resistance research effort. These named varieties provide more specific planting information than the broad label “landrace”; their cup expression also depends on the growing site and processing.

Processing

Cherries are sorted by flotation before eco-pulping removes their skins. The parchment coffee ferments for two to three days to loosen the mucilage, then soaks for 12 hours. Drying takes seven to ten days on raised beds, followed by another sorting stage before dry milling.

Washed processing can emphasize clarity and definition in the cup, with the final result also shaped by growing conditions, drying, and roasting.
